messages:
maya: Heads-up — multiple customers reported p99 jump after canary rollout (v2.5.0) around 2026-03-25T14:12Z. Dash shows p99 160ms -> ~2.5s on streaming/generate. Example trace id=abc123 shows ~1.9s queuing on hotpath. Link: https://console.redwood/perf/trace/abc123

sam: saw it on dashboards too. Canary cluster p99 spikes coincide with kernel-selector changes. Affected models: rdx-l1-quant, rdx-chat-small. :eyes:

tomas: I pulled flamegraphs from canary nodes — CPU is steady but goroutine queues spike. Looks like per-request kernel selection is running multiple probes and blocking. stack: `ResolveCandidate() -> probeKernel() -> wait` shows repeated probe latency.

maya: @devon did the kernel selector experiment land in canary? deploy-bot shows a config patch earlier.

devon: yep, I rolled an experiment: `kernel_selector.timeout_ms=200` (was 50) for better stability when kernels are slow-loading. The idea was to avoid immediate fallback churn, but seems to be causing longer probe waits under cold KV cache.

maya: can someone repro locally quickly? we should validate before rolling forward.

tomas: repro steps I used:
```
# quick repro (canary-like):
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do \
  curl -s -H "x-tenant: acme" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"test"}' https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
Run with model header `x-model: rdx-l1-quant` at QPS ~50. On my local canary mimic I see p99 ~2.1s and logs showing `kernel_probe_count=3` per request.

devon: reproduced. Logs: `selector.go:172 probeAttempt=2 probeDuration=230ms probeReason=fallback`. Selector is trying multiple kernel probes because cached kernel not picked (KV key miss) and timeout forces additional probes.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) rollback kernel_selector.timeout change in canary to previous value, 2) apply a runtime hotfix that short-circuits probe loop when KV cache reports "warming" (fast-path), 3) emergency routing for affected tenants to prefer stable cluster while we validate. If rollback green, promote hotfix.

devon: starting rollback now. deploy-bot:rollback started for runtime-canary v2.5.0 -> 2.4.3. Will update traffic-split to 0% canary.

maya: also toggling routing for tenants: `routing.policy=prefer-stable` for acme and beta-corp. That should reduce user impact.

infra-bot: traffic-split update applied by devon at 2026-03-25T14:28:05Z — canary traffic set to 0%.

sam: post-rollback numbers: p95 back to baseline, p99 improved from ~2.5s -> 180ms within 3 minutes. Small residual tail (200-300ms) remaining for a subset — likely KV-warmup.

maya: action items:
- devon: revert config in canary and prepare hotfix PR with selector fast-path (add unit + integration test).
- tomas: add `kernel_probe_count` and `kernel_probe_time_ms` metrics per-request and dashboard. Alert if probe_count > 3 for any 1m window.
- sam: coordinate rollback verification and schedule canary re-roll with hotfix.
- infra: document emergency routing steps and add a runbook entry for kernel-selector regressions.

devon: noted. I'll open PR and tag reviewers. Will also include a short-circuit: if KV_cache_ready==false and probe_count>1 then prefer stable kernel candidate instead of full probe.

maya: TL;DR — root cause appears to be increased kernel_selector probe timeout + codepath that triggers repeated probes on cold KV state. Rollback + short-circuit + emergency routing mitigated customer impact. Follow-ups: add tests, metrics, and an alert for selector probe anomalies.

sam: thanks team. keeping thread open for 30m to confirm no regressions. Ping here when canary re-roll planned. :thumbsup:
